label: “critical thinking abilities”
measured: A survey score. The instrument is not named in the abstract, and the full text is unreachable from here (MDPI returns 403 to automated requests), so what was actually administered cannot be verified.
note: The most-cited source for the erosion claim. Also carries a correction notice whose content is not retrievable.

label: “critical reasoning”
measured: Expert rubric ratings of 450 written responses produced under four conditions. A performance measure of the output, scored by humans against a rubric.
isct: yes — and the only performance measure here
design: Cross-country experiment, 4 conditions (human-only, unguided AI, guided AI, AI-only)
note: Same author as the row above, different construct and different method. Found offloading 'without improving reasoning quality' — an absence of gain, not a decline.

label: “enaction of critical thinking” and “effort” of doing it
measured: Per-task self-report about whether the person thinks they engaged critically on that task, plus qualitative coding of 936 examples into information verification, response integration, task stewardship.
note: Frames the change as a shift in the NATURE of critical thinking, not a loss of capacity. Often cited as if it showed a loss.

label: “critical thinking”
measured: One of five outcomes tracked across three timepoints. The instrument is not named in the abstract and the full text is unreachable (Wiley 403).
note: Reports critical thinking 'remained stable' — a null, in the only longitudinal design in this set.

label: does not claim to measure critical thinking
measured: How much correct and incorrect information a student pulled from an expert-written and a ChatGPT-written article into their own writing; plus metacognitive bias and epistemic beliefs.
isct: NO — source integration, not critical thinking
design: Two-condition experiment (independent vs ChatGPT-assisted writing), 49 per arm
note: Cited in erosion discussions because it bears on evaluating AI output. It measures a different thing.

label: does not use the phrase at all
measured: Verified against the full text: zero occurrences of 'critical thinking'. The T3 outcomes are four self-rated constructs — subsequent autonomous capability, creativity, deep processing, independent judgment — each a 4-item perception scale.
design: Three-wave time-lagged survey, waves 2 weeks apart
note: The strongest design in this set — and it measures perceptions of one's own capability, not capability.

label: “perceived erosion of professional skills”
measured: A self-report scale inside a mediation model running from entrepreneurial orientation through GenAI dependence to perceived skill erosion.
isct: NO — perceived skill, not critical thinking
design: Cross-sectional survey with sequential mediation model
note: Measures a belief about one's own skills. No cognitive outcome is measured.
